dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For each natural number n, this is the type of n-by-n real matrices indexed by Fin n in both coordinates.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: It is matrix-vector multiplication: for a vector v, (Av)_i = sum over all j in Fin n of A_ij v_j.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: It is the residual map r(v) = b - Av, with subtraction performed coordinatewise.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The old and new residuals in the theorem are b - Ax and b - A xNext, respectively.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006

binders: n is an arbitrary natural number, including zero.
A is an arbitrary real n-by-n matrix.
b, x, correction, xNext, rhat, deltaR, and deltaX are arbitrary real n-vectors.
epsilonR, epsilonU, w, and omega are arbitrary real numbers.
conclusions: ||b - A xNext||_2 ≤ w ||b - Ax||_2 + (epsilonR + epsilonU + omega)(||b||_2 + ||A||_F ||xNext||_2).
mathematical_definitions: The coordinate index set is Fin n, identified with {0, 1, ..., n-1}; it is empty when n = 0.
Vector addition and subtraction are coordinatewise.
For a vector v, (Av)_i = sum over j in Fin n of A_ij v_j.
The residual at v is r(v) = b - Av.
For a vector v, ||v||_2 = sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of v_i^2).
For a real matrix A, ||A||_F is its Frobenius norm, equivalently sqrt(sum over i and j in Fin n of A_ij^2).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite dimension n, every real n-by-n matrix A, all listed real n-vectors, and all real parameters epsilonR, epsilonU, w, and omega, suppose rhat is exactly the old residual b - Ax perturbed by deltaR, and xNext is exactly x plus correction plus deltaX. Suppose the defect rhat - A correction is bounded by w times the old residual norm plus omega times the scale ||b||_2 + ||A||_F||xNext||_2; deltaR and deltaX satisfy their stated relative norm bounds; ||x||_2 does not exceed ||xNext||_2; and epsilonR and epsilonU are nonnegative. Then the new residual norm is at most w times the old residual norm plus epsilonR + epsilonU + omega times the scale ||b||_2 + ||A||_F||xNext||_2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement is a universally quantified implication. It does not assert that vectors satisfying the hypotheses exist; whenever the hypotheses are inconsistent, the implication is vacuously true.
The dimension n may be zero. In that case all coordinate sets are empty, all vector and matrix norms are zero, and the conclusion reduces to 0 ≤ 0.
No nonsingularity, invertibility, symmetry, definiteness, rank, or conditioning assumption is imposed on A.
The matrix norm is specifically the Frobenius norm, not the induced spectral or operator 2-norm.
epsilonR and epsilonU are only required to be nonnegative; no smallness or upper-bound assumption is encoded.
No sign restriction is imposed on w or omega. Negative choices may make the correction-defect hypothesis impossible and hence make an instance vacuous.
The relative deltaR bound uses ||x||_2, whereas the deltaX bound is relative to ||xNext||_2.
The inequality ||x||_2 ≤ ||xNext||_2 is an explicit hypothesis rather than a consequence of the update equation.
The vector named correction has no independent size or accuracy bound; only the norm of rhat - A correction is controlled.

All equalities and inequalities concern exact mathematical real numbers. No floating-point format, rounding operation, algorithm, convergence claim, exact solution, forward-error bound, or computed-data semantics is encoded.
